prerequisites: Ability for abstract and logical thinking.

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have knowledge of symmetric and asymmetric cryptographic methods.
They can decide under which conditions certain ciphers are used in practice and how the security parameters are to be chosen.
They are familiar with the mathematical foundations on which current cryptographic methods are based.

Through the description of selected practically relevant ciphers, such as the AES or RSA algorithm and the Diffie-Hellman key exchange, students will also achieve an algorithmic and technical understanding of modern cryptography.
They are able to argumentatively defend a specific solution.
Students can acquire language competencies in the scientific language English through the bilingual e-learning offer.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to modern applied cryptography and basics of IT security
Focus on cryptographic methods, necessary mathematics, and interaction of cryptography and IT security
Description of historical symmetric ciphers (Caesar cipher, affine cipher, One Time Pad)
Current symmetric methods (Advanced Encryption Standard, Data Encryption Standard, Stream ciphers)
Relevant basics of number theory (Rings of integers, Groups, Fields, Discrete logarithms, Euclidean algorithm, Euler's totient function)
Algorithmic introduction to asymmetric cryptographic methods
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon successful passing of the module exam. The exam is a 120-minute written examination.
